name: Riverside Walk
gainNote: Round-trip ascent derived from the NPS accessibility survey’s 154.2 ft outbound gain and 48.5 ft outbound loss.
access: Begin past the restrooms at Temple of Sinawava. Turn around where the paved path ends, before entering The Narrows.
description: Follow the Virgin River beneath Zion Canyon’s sandstone walls on a concrete path with sandy sections. This riverside hike ends at the Narrows approach; it does not include river hiking.
turnaround: Turn around at the end of the paved path; return on the same path to Temple of Sinawava.
distanceConvention: 2.0 mi is the complete return hike, using the NPS accessibility survey’s 1 mi outbound measurement.
statsNote: The park overview also lists 2.2 mi and 57 ft elevation change. Elevation change is not cumulative ascent; this itinerary uses the survey convention and 203 ft derived return ascent.
geometryReview: Current NPS source segments, junction order, return path, endpoint access and distance were checked against the stored trace. This is a source review, not a field inspection.

name: Bear Lake Loop
gainNote: Elevation gain is published by NPS for the loop.
surface: Firm packed gravel, wooden bridges, and log steps
access: Start at the east lakeshore junction, a short walk from Bear Lake Trailhead. The short parking-area approach is outside the loop distance. Check Bear Lake Road access and timed entry with the park.
description: Circle an alpine lake framed by spruce and fir, with views toward the surrounding peaks. Gravel, log steps and wooden bridges make this a walking loop rather than a uniformly smooth path.
turnaround: Complete the lakeshore loop back to the east lakeshore junction. No separate summit or turnaround is included.
distanceConvention: 0.6 mi is the lakeshore loop only; the short parking-area approach is excluded.
statsNote: The corridor guide lists 0.6 mi and 71 ft gain. The hiking index lists 0.7 mi for a lollipop-style route; an older accessibility guide lists 0.5 mi and 20 ft. Those start/measurement conventions are not used here.
geometryReview: Current NPS source segments, junction order, return path, endpoint access and distance were checked against the stored trace. This is a source review, not a field inspection.

name: Flattop Mountain
gainNote: NPS publishes 2,849 ft of gain to the destination. Extra ascent on the return is unverified.
surface: Earth in NPS GIS; exposed alpine terrain above treeline
access: Follow the Flattop route from Bear Lake to the Tonahutu/North Inlet junction, then return the same way. Check the park’s trail conditions and Bear Lake Road access.

name: Hall of Mosses
trailheadName: Hoh Rain Forest · Hall of Mosses trail entrance
gainNote: Elevation gain is published by NPS for the loop.
surface: Compacted gravel with rocky stretches and steps
access: Start near the Hoh Rain Forest Visitor Center. The trail crosses Taft Creek. Check Hoh Road and facility access with the park.
description: Walk beneath moss-draped bigleaf maples and conifers in the Hoh Rain Forest. The compacted-gravel route has roots, rocks and steps, crosses Taft Creek, and includes a short approach before the loop.
turnaround: Follow the full Hall of Mosses loop, then retrace the entrance approach to the mapped start near the visitor center.
distanceConvention: 0.8 mi is the NPS Hoh brochure loop convention; the mapped entrance approach and return bring the GIS trace to 0.86 mi.
statsNote: The Hoh brochure lists 100 ft gain. The accessibility survey measures a longer route from a different start; its distance is not substituted for this brochure itinerary.
geometryReview: Current NPS source segments, junction order, return path, endpoint access and distance were checked against the stored trace. This is a source review, not a field inspection.

name: Lower Yosemite Fall Trail
trailheadName: Lower Yosemite Fall · east junction near shuttle stop 6
gainNote: The National Park Service publishes about 50 ft of elevation gain for the full loop.
access: Start on the loop near the Lower Yosemite Fall shuttle stop. Follow the path to the footbridge and return on the opposite side of the loop. The shuttle-stop approach is outside the loop.
description: Walk through Yosemite Valley forest to the footbridge below Lower Yosemite Fall. The paved loop offers views of the falls, but spray can make the bridge area slippery and the waterfall can be seasonal.
turnaround: Complete the loop across the viewing footbridge and return by the other branch to the east junction near shuttle stop 6.
distanceConvention: 1.0 mi is the complete NPS loop itinerary. The mapped start is the east junction; extra travel from a parking space or shuttle is excluded.
statsNote: The NPS trail guide lists 1 mi and approximately 50 ft gain; the assembled GIS trace measures 0.97 mi.
geometryReview: Current NPS source segments, junction order, return path, endpoint access and distance were checked against the stored trace. This is a source review, not a field inspection.

name: Limberlost Trail
trailheadName: Limberlost parking area · Skyline Drive mile 43
gainNote: The National Park Service publishes 130 ft of elevation gain for the full loop.
access: Begin at the Limberlost parking area, Skyline Drive mile 43. Take the greenstone path to the right; complete the loop to the neighboring access points in the same parking area.
description: Explore a forest loop on crushed greenstone with benches and interpretive features. Grades vary along this accessible-design route, so review the park’s detailed access information for your party.
turnaround: Follow the full loop back to the neighboring access point in the same Limberlost parking area.
distanceConvention: 1.3 mi is the complete loop from the Limberlost parking area at Skyline Drive mile 43.
statsNote: The NPS hike page lists 130 ft gain. The GIS line measures 1.34 mi and has neighboring parking-area endpoints about 13.5 m apart; no connecting line is invented.
geometryReview: Current NPS source segments, junction order, return path, endpoint access and distance were checked against the stored trace. This is a source review, not a field inspection.

name: Desert Discovery Trail
trailheadName: Desert Discovery Trailhead · Tucson Mountain District
gainNote: The NPS accessibility survey measured 25.8 ft of loop gain, rounded to 26 ft.
access: Begin at the dedicated Desert Discovery parking area on Kinney Road, about one mile northwest of Red Hills Visitor Center. The loop returns to neighboring access points in the same parking area.
description: Explore Sonoran Desert plants on a short paved interpretive loop in the Tucson Mountain District. The route has changing slopes and little protection from desert heat; carry water and check current park guidance.
turnaround: Complete the paved loop to the neighboring access point in the same Desert Discovery parking area.
distanceConvention: 0.4 mi is the NPS accessibility-survey loop measurement, rounded from the mapped 0.38 mi trace.
statsNote: Generic park summaries also describe this as 0.5 mi. This itinerary follows the specific accessibility survey and its 25.8 ft cumulative gain, rounded to 26 ft; parking-area endpoints are about 13.5 m apart.
geometryReview: Current NPS source segments, junction order, return path, endpoint access and distance were checked against the stored trace. This is a source review, not a field inspection.
